architecture: Scheme semantic ownership; mandatory modern-C foundation; explicit execution/memory/control/FFI contracts.
C-to-Zig is a conditional implementation evolution, not a second required runtime.
modern-c: Typed generated interfaces, native requests, physical layout and actual retirement of implicit macro/C decisions.
Retain the C backend, C ABI, FFI and embedding as core capabilities.
zig: Named implementation replacements and their incremental support/toolchain/resource benefit.
No adoption from syntax, C interoperability or common modernization gains alone.
runtime: VM/worker/context/participant separation, memory sharing, ownership, requests and resource last use.
Source SMP support, configured profile and native qualification are different evidence.
gc: Allocation, initialization, roots, barriers, promotion, copying capacity, weak/finalizer and worker contracts.
Generational/concurrent candidates require every real writer and root contributor to close.
control: Frames, tail transfer, dynamic environments, general continuations and researched one-shot resumptions.
No automatic capture of native C frames or duplication of linear native resources.
ffi: Borrowed/retained values, owner attachment, blocking/reentry, callbacks, cancellation and shutdown drain.
The Tcl studies are stress cases, not the whole modernization program.
compiler: GVM/high semantic export, closure/effect legality, MLIR/LLVM lowering and code/metadata lifetime.
LLVM/MLIR services consume Gambit semantics; they do not issue runtime ownership authority.
toolchain: Darwin/GCC inputs, argv/configuration, observation, build cache, AOT and artifact invalidation.
Cache reuse is not fresh module/context instantiation or native semantic acceptance.
research: Questions, arguments, source/paper bindings, counterexamples, gates and evidence-class distinctions.
A model validation is not a runtime proof, benchmark or satisfied research gate.

manualTaxonomyRefinement.reason: Own semantic compiler, toolchain, FFI and shared runtime studies in their actual subsystem, not a catch-all research category; IDs preserved.

relocationPolicy: Org identities preserved; file links/includes/setup paths rebased; formal source remains under models; old evidence unchanged.
